result.title: Preface
result.summary: An August 4, 2023 request for proposals for deferred compensation services covering administration and recordkeeping, marketing/enrollment/education, investment management, and custodial trustee services. The plan administration RFP outlines general information, including background, county objectives, scope, proposal submission and format, evaluation and selection, and contract term. Section I covers contractual requirements, regulations, and model plan specifications. Section II requests information on trustee services. Section III covers the administrative service agency/financial organization and company background. Section IV addresses marketing, enrollment and education, administration, recordkeeping systems, and service fees and expenses. Section V covers fund offerings and investment flexibility. Section VI addresses conversion-service experience and process. Exhibits provide investment performance, a fee schedule, and plan data.

result.title: GENERAL INFORMATION
result.summary: The Monroe County Deferred Compensation Plan is a defined-contribution plan for County employees, exempt under IRC Section 457(b), governed by New York State Deferred Compensation Board rules, and based on the State Model Plan. It supplements pensions and Social Security by promoting retirement savings, broad participation, and individual education; it also includes an OBRA plan for part-time seasonal workers. At December 31, 2022, the main plan had 4,398 participants and $308.7 million in assets; the OBRA plan had 536 participants and $926,785. Annual contributions were $13.29 million plus rollovers, and the median account balance was $26,191. The County had about 4,100 full-time employees and one dedicated educator, conducting roughly 100 group meetings and 1,000 individual seminars. County objectives are to improve employees’ financial position and retirement income through a planned program; ensure Social Security compliance for seasonal and part-time work; provide hardship-withdrawal consultation and a qualified trustee; and support the Deferred Compensation Committee’s statutory duties and decisions.

result.title: Deferred Compensation Plan RFP Scope and Submission
result.summary: Monroe County seeks proposals from qualified administrative service agencies and financial organizations to provide trust services, plan administration, recordkeeping, and/or funding products for its eligible deferred compensation plan. Submit one original and six copies to the specified Monroe County purchasing office by 3:00 p.m. September 8, 2023. Written or emailed questions must reach Walter Webert by 3:00 p.m. August 18; any answers will be distributed by addendum to RFP recipients by August 25. Contact with other County or Committee members about the RFP is prohibited unless authorized in writing and may result in disqualification. Late proposals will not be considered; proposers are responsible for timely delivery, and the County is not responsible for lost or late submissions.

result.title: Form and Substance
result.summary: The RFP relies on the New York State Deferred Compensation Board’s Regulations (effective June 15, 2011) and Model Plan, amended through December 11, 2020, available at deferredcompboard.ny.gov; noncompliance may result in rejection. Proposals must include a completed questionnaire restating and answering every item in Sections I–V, answer all Section I contractual requirements, follow RFP specifications, and mark inapplicable items “not applicable.” Separate complete responses are required from any recordkeeping provider that is neither the Financial Organization’s parent nor subsidiary. Include a signed transmittal letter on official letterhead from an authorized company official, committing to perform the services and affirming compliance with the Regulations and Model Plan. Submission waives claims for damages arising from misunderstandings, misrepresentations, missing information, or nonselection, and accepts the entire RFP and attachments. Proposal and presentation commitments must be incorporated into resulting contracts. The proposer bears all proposal, presentation, and negotiation costs. Follow the prescribed uniform format and be concise; excessive submissions may disqualify.

result.title: Evaluation Criteria
result.summary:
Evaluation Criteria
In selecting, we will use criteria which comply with the requirements of the Regulations, including Section 9003.3(a)(1 through 7) of the Regulations.
All qualified proposals, sought in conjunction with the requirements of Section 9003.2 of the Regulations, will be evaluated and awards made to the Proposer or Proposers whose bid is determined to be in the best interest of the plan participants.

result.title: Selection Process
result.summary: The regulations authorize an appointed committee to act on the organization’s behalf. Before a committee-selected contract or agreement takes effect, it must submit the selected proposer’s name and a certification signed by the chief executive and chief legal officers to the New York State Civil Service Commission President. Contracts cannot be awarded until 90 days after notice is published in the State Register and local paper. Oral presentations may be requested, and awards will be communicated in writing. The timetable is: proposals due September 8, 2023; review by September 29; subcommittee selection by October 27; full committee selection by November 9; services operational January 1, 2024. The organization may reject proposals, establish a plan through permitted methods, negotiate directly with multiple proposers, or change the process, project scope, or response requirements. Solicitation or exclusive negotiation rights do not guarantee acceptance: final terms are negotiated and require County approval, and negotiations may be suspended or ended if deemed unproductive.

result.title: Term of Contract
result.summary:
Term of Contract
Pursuant to Section 9003.5(a) of the Regulations, we expect to enter into a written contractual arrangement(s) of up to five (5) years in duration. The contract shall be subject to periodic review by the Committee. The Committee may cancel the contract at the end of any contract year upon providing the investment management and/or the administrative services agency with 30 days advance notice in writing. All contracts and agreements entered into shall impose no penalties or surrender charges for the transfer of assets or responsibilities on expiration of the contract or agreement. Upon the expiration or termination of any contract(s) or agreement(s), the committee shall follow procedures set forth in the Regulations in Part 9003 for awarding new contracts and entering into new agreements.

result.title: CONTRACTUAL REQUIREMENTS
result.summary: For every specification, indicate agree or disagree; explain any disagreement and offer alternatives where applicable, with no elaboration or qualification for agreement unless requested. Regulatory requirements cover provider eligibility (registered investment adviser, bank, or multistate-qualified insurer) and subsidiary certification; cooperation with the deferred compensation committee and, if applicable, the trust and trustee, with funding contracts issued to and retained by the trustee; compliance with Section 9001.4, especially prohibiting annuity payouts; required bonding and insurance; fiduciary duties and indemnification; written, compliant proposals disclosing all fees; written, competitively awarded contracts limited to five years without transfer penalties; no other service providers; restrictions on long-term/life-based annuities and life insurance; confidentiality and no non-plan solicitation or products; quarterly participant statements and annual fee disclosures; and contracts incorporating the Regulations and Model Plan. Model Plan requirements include a $260 minimum deferral, investment according to participant directions within two business days, and holding each participant’s entire account value, including annuities, in trust by the trustee.

result.title: Trustee Services Proposal Requirements
result.summary: Section II of a Plan Administration RFP invites Financial Organizations seeking trustee status to respond; others may skip to the next applicable section. It explains regulatory requirements for holding plan assets in compliant trusts and the option of using an outside Financial Organization. Respondents should provide firm and contact details; experience serving New York municipalities’ 457(b) plans; trust-service scope, fees, costs, and compensation disclosures; and whether they also intend to bid as Administrative Service Agency, including the effect on fees and the need to answer Sections III and IV. They must address fiduciary acknowledgments, required bonding and any costs borne by the plan, provision and compliance of a sample trust agreement, restrictions on assignment or delegation to another trustee, and proposed performance guarantees. The page ends with the Section III heading.

result.title: ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICE AGENCY/ FINANCIAL ORGANIZATION
result.summary: The RFP seeks responses from firms proposing to serve as the Administrative Service Agency and/or Financial Organization (excluding trustee); respondents should mark inapplicable items “Not Applicable” and explain. It requests firm and contact details; company history and experience with public-sector 457(b) plans, especially in New York since 1985; current plan counts, including New York plans; any client terminations in the past five years; and ten comparable client references with contact, participant, deferral, asset, and service-tenure details, preferably including five similarly sized New York plans. It also asks about professional liability coverage, the latest audited financial statement, SAS 70 or equivalent internal-control assurance, relevant past or pending litigation, and Financial Organization ratings from A.M. Best, S&P, Moody’s, and Fitch, including any ratings below A- in the past five years or an explanation for having none. Respondents should describe potential performance guarantees and other information distinguishing their firm.

result.title: SERVICES
key_items: A. Services offered to the Plan Sponsor
Recordkeeping System; Fees and Expenses for Services
result.summary: The RFP asks prospective administrative service agencies to address marketing, employee communications, promotional materials, branding, costs, compliance education, group and individual enrollment sessions, retiree education, investment allocation, follow-up, continuing education, representative licensing, qualifications, staffing, compensation, monitoring, experience, solicitation safeguards, and performance guarantees. It also requests Plan Sponsor services, including dedicated support, model-plan revisions, loans, Roth 457 accounts, tax withholding/reporting, and reports. Participant services include investment guidance and managed accounts, high-balance planning, phone and online systems, language support, security, statement frequency, permitted settlement options, and transfers between providers. Recordkeeping questions cover systems, transaction controls and audits, software, data processing and security, disaster recovery, subcontracting, payroll interfaces, certifications, and costs. Respondents must itemize fees and explain how trustee services, audits, legal expenses, and committee costs affect them, and compare investment revenue-sharing with per-participant charges, including treatment of excess revenue and participant credits.

result.title: INVESTMENTS
result.summary: The RFP asks financial organizations to provide current-quarter details on every investment option, including product type, objectives, portfolio statistics, allocation, top holdings, industry diversification, sample contracts and prospectuses. For fixed options, describe five years of rates, assets, rating methods, rate-setting practices, expenses and revenue above surrender rates. Supply specified spreadsheets showing variable-option returns across requested periods and all fees and charges. Explain no-cost OBRA arrangements for part-time/seasonal employees, brokerage windows, performance guarantees, transfer restrictions, penalties and any additional charges or limits. The conversion section applies only to non-incumbent administrative agencies. It requests takeover histories for 457(b) plans, including providers, dates, assets, participants, timelines and staffing; a full transition process, schedule and costs; on-site support and personnel; effects of becoming sole administrator; three recent references, preferably in New York; and proposed performance guarantees.

result.title: Plan Conversion Services
result.summary: The page asks bidders to identify any additional charges or limitations, then outlines conversion-service questions for administrative service agencies taking over a plan from another provider; incumbent providers may skip this section. Bidders must describe their history of successful Code Section 457(b) plan takeovers, including client, takeover date, former provider, assets, participants, transition duration, staffing, and other relevant details. They must explain transition activities, timeline, and costs to the plan or participants; describe on-site support and who provides it; discuss the effects of becoming sole administrator, such as fee reductions or added services; provide three recent transition references, preferably in New York; and state what performance guarantees they would consider.
